function.name: execute_device_command
function.description: Execute a generic command or API call on a device. This is a flexible tool for operations not covered by specific tools. Use only when other tools don't provide the needed functionality.

device_name.description: Name of the device

command.description: Command to execute or API endpoint to call (e.g., 'show version', '/api/system/info')

parameters.description: Optional parameters for the command or API call as key-value pairs

function.name: search_documentation
function.description: Search device documentation, CLI references, and API guides to answer 'how-to' questions and provide command syntax help. Use this when users ask questions about device features, configuration procedures, or need to understand command syntax. IMPORTANT: You MUST cite sources for all information retrieved from documentation. Use the format [Source: filename, Page X] for every fact or command you provide. If no relevant documentation is found, explicitly state that the information is not available in the current documentation and suggest where the user might find it.

query.description: Search query describing what information is needed. Examples: 'How to configure PoE power limits', 'Cable diagnostics commands', 'VLAN configuration syntax', 'API endpoint for port status'

device_model.description: Optional device model to filter results. Use the model name from device metadata (e.g., 'SM8TBT2SA', 'SmartSwitch'). Model aliases are handled automatically. If not specified, searches all available documentation.

doc_type.description: Type of documentation to search. Use 'cli_reference' for CLI commands, 'api_guide' for REST API information, 'web_guide' for web UI help, or 'all' to search all documentation types. Default is 'all'.

max_results.description: Maximum number of documentation sections to return (1-10). Default is 5.

function.name: diagnose_port_issues
function.description: Perform comprehensive diagnostics to troubleshoot why a port is down or having issues, AND to view syslog events and recent activity for a port. USE THIS TOOL when users ask about: recent events, syslog, event log, port history, port issues, connectivity problems, or port diagnostics. This tool analyzes multiple data sources including: current port status, interface error counters, PoE status (if applicable), cable diagnostics test results, and historical syslog events. It automatically detects patterns like link flapping, PoE power cycling, error storms, and configuration-related issues. Use this tool when users ask about port down problems, connectivity issues, or need help diagnosing why a device connected to a port isn't working. Example queries: 'What are recent events on port 4?', 'Show syslog for port 5', 'Why is port 5 down?', 'Diagnose connectivity issue on port 3', 'What's wrong with the camera on port 7?', 'Port 2 keeps flapping', 'Show event log for port 1'

device_name.description: Name of the device (switch) to diagnose (e.g., 'poe1', 'switch1', 'issw')

port.description: Port identifier to diagnose. Can be in various formats: '5', '1/5', 'Gi1/5', 'GigabitEthernet1/5'

time_range.description: How far back to analyze syslog history. Options: '1h' (1 hour), '6h' (6 hours), '24h' (24 hours - default), '7d' (7 days). Longer ranges help detect intermittent issues.

function.name: get_camera_detections
function.description: Query what a camera is currently detecting, or look up detection history. Use mode='live' to sample the stream right now (e.g. 'what does the entrance camera see?'). Use mode='history' to query the SQLite log for past detections (e.g. 'has anyone been at the loading bay in the last 10 minutes?'). When the user mentions a specific camera by name or location, supply camera_id. camera1 (Entrance Camera) does object detection — available COCO labels: person, backpack, suitcase, handbag, car, truck, motorcycle, bicycle, bottle, laptop, cell-phone, knife, scissors, etc. camera2 (Loading Bay Camera) does gesture/pose detection — available labels: left-hand-raised, right-hand-raised. Use the appropriate labels based on which camera the user is asking about.

mode.description: Use 'live' to sample the camera now. Use 'history' to query stored detections.

camera_id.description: Optional camera ID to filter by (e.g. 'camera1', 'camera2'). Omit to query all cameras.

labels.description: Optional list of object labels to filter by. Examples: ['person'], ['person', 'backpack'], ['car', 'truck']

duration.description: Live mode only: seconds to sample. Default 5, max 30.

seconds_ago.description: History mode only: how many seconds back to query. Examples: 60 (1 min), 600 (10 min), 3600 (1 hour), 86400 (1 day).

function.name: get_network_events
function.description: Query recent network events from the PoE switch syslog feed. Use this when users ask about network activity, switch events, PoE events, link state changes, authentication failures, or any switch log history. Examples: 'what happened on the network in the last 5 minutes?', 'any PoE events recently?', 'show link-down events', 'did anything happen on the switch today?'

seconds_ago.description: How many seconds back to query. Examples: 300 (5 min), 3600 (1 hour), 86400 (1 day).

groups.description: Optional list of event group names to filter by. Available groups: LINK-UP, LINK-DOWN, POE-PD-ON, POE-PD-OFF, POE-FAULT, POE-OVERLOAD, AUTH-FAILED, COLD-START, WARM-START, CONFIG-CHANGE, STP, LOOP, PORT-SECURITY, OTHER.

function.name: calibrate_cable_baseline
function.description: Calibrate and store a cable length baseline for a switch port. Run this when a cable is healthy and connected to establish a reference length. Later, diagnose_port_issues will compare measured lengths against the baseline to identify where a cable break or disconnect occurred (near-end, midpoint, or far-end). Only works when cable test result is OK/Normal.

device_name.description: Switch name (e.g., 'poesw1')
